title: Frontend Development Libraries
description: Learn the core ideas behind modern UI libraries like React.

sections.title: Component-Based UI
sections.content: Modern frontend libraries build interfaces out of small, reusable components. Each component describes a piece of UI and can be combined with others to build a full page. Components can be written as functions that return UI markup.

quiz.question: What is a component in a frontend library?
Why are interfaces divided into components?
choices: To make code reusable and easier to maintain
To prevent users from interacting with the page

quiz.question: What does a component generally describe?
choices: A piece of the user interface

sections.title: State & Props
sections.content: Props pass data into a component from its parent and are read-only. State is data a component manages itself and can change over time, causing the UI to re-render.

quiz.question: What are props used for?
choices: Passing data into a component from its parent

quiz.question: Can a component directly modify the props it receives?
choices: Only when the component has no state

quiz.question: What is state?
choices: Data managed by a component that can change over time

sections.title: Hooks Basics
sections.content: Hooks let function components use features like state. useState returns a value and a function to update it; updating state triggers a re-render.

quiz.question: What are Hooks used for in React?
choices: Allowing function components to use React features

quiz.question: What does useState return?
choices: A value and a function to update it

quiz.question: What typically happens when state is updated?

exam.question: What is a component in a frontend library?
What is a major benefit of component-based UI?
choices: It eliminates the need for JavaScript
It removes the need for HTML-like markup

exam.question: How can multiple components be used to create a page?
choices: They can be combined to build a larger interface
Only one component can exist on a page
Components can only be used for styling
Components must always be separate applications

exam.question: What does a function component generally return?
Why is component reuse useful?
choices: The same UI logic can be used in multiple places
It removes the need for application logic

exam.question: What are props?
choices: Data passed into a component from its parent
Data stored permanently in the browser

exam.question: Are props normally modified directly by the component receiving them?
choices: Yes, they should always be modified

exam.question: In `Welcome(props)`, what does `props` represent?
choices: The data passed into the component

exam.question: Which component would correctly display a name passed through props?
What is state?
choices: Data that a component manages and can change over time
Read-only data passed from a parent

exam.question: What is one important difference between props and state?
choices: Props are passed into a component, while state is managed by the component
Props are CSS while state is HTML
Props are functions while state is always a string

exam.question: What can happen when a component's state changes?
choices: The component can re-render with the updated state

exam.question: What are React Hooks?
choices: Features that allow function components to use React capabilities

exam.question: Which Hook is used to add state to a function component?
What does `useState(0)` initially provide as the state value?
In `const [count, setCount] = useState(0)`, what is `count`?
In `const [count, setCount] = useState(0)`, what is `setCount`?
choices: A function used to update the state

exam.question: What does `setCount(count + 1)` do?
choices: Updates the count state to its current value plus one

exam.question: Why does updating state matter to the UI?
choices: Updating state can cause the component to re-render
Updating state permanently reloads the browser
Updating state changes CSS files on the server

exam.question: Which statement best summarizes the three concepts in this lesson?
choices: Components build reusable UI, props pass data into components, and state manages changing data
Components are CSS files, props are database tables, and state is HTML
Components replace JavaScript, props replace CSS, and state replaces HTML
Components can only display text, props create layouts, and state stores files
